confirmed.title: H205-10 is partly fixed
confirmed.problem: lib/cardOnFileWebhook.ts:181 flags only when inv.autoCharge?.reference !== reference. The network-error path is fixed because no reference is stored. The 'processing' path from the original trigger is not fixed: chargeFee (and reconcileFeeCharge) record autoCharge {status:'failed', reference: pi.id}, and feeFallback tells staff to send the invoice. When the client pays the invoice link (invoicePay only patches status, not autoCharge), the later payment_intent.succeeded has reference === autoCharge.reference. No flag is raised, markFeeInvoicePaid returns false, and the double payment goes unnoticed. A void works the same way. Fix: treat the charge as ours only when the reference matches AND autoCharge.status is 'succeeded' or 'charging'; otherwise flagFeeChargeToCheck.
confirmed.trigger: see round 1 finding H205-10
confirmed.fix: cardOnFileWebhook.ts:181: treat the charge as ours only when inv.autoCharge?.reference === reference AND inv.autoCharge.status is 'succeeded' or 'charging'. Otherwise, when inv.status is paid or void, call flagFeeChargeToCheck. Add a test: processing outcome, then invoice paid by link, then the webhook succeeds, and assert the 'Check charge' insight exists.
confirmed.skepticReason: The trigger is real. chargeFee (cardOnFile.ts:577-585) handles a 'processing' PaymentIntent by calling _feeChargeOutcome with outcome 'failed' and reference: pi.id. reconcileFeeCharge (cardOnFile.ts:660-668) does the same for a found PI in any other non-succeeded state. _feeChargeOutcome:537 stores autoCharge {status:'failed', reference: pi.id} and feeFallback tells staff to send the invoice and tells the client one will follow. invoicePay.settleInvoice never touches autoCharge (git grep finds autoCharge only in cardOnFile.ts, cardOnFileWebhook.ts, sessions.ts and money.ts), so after the client pays by link (or staff void), inv.autoCharge.reference still equals the PI id. When payment_intent.succeeded then arrives, settleFee at cardOnFileWebhook.ts:181 sees reference === autoCharge.reference, so it skips the flag. markFeeInvoicePaid:231 returns false with no alert. The client has paid twice and nobody is told. Round 1 named the 'processing' PI in its trigger, so the round 2 fix does not do what it claims.

confirmed.title: When a payment made after the no-show covers the fee, staff are still told to send the fee invoice and the client is told it is coming
confirmed.problem: _claimFeeCharge re-reads the paid amount, which is correct. But when autoChargeDecision refuses because the client has since paid at least the fee ('the client already paid at least the fee'), or because the charge is now more than fee minus paid, the code takes the generic skip() path, and skip() calls feeFallback. feeFallback adds a 'Send invoice X: the no-show fee was not charged' insight, logs activity, emails the team and emails the client 'invoice to follow' for the full inv.amountCents. The draft invoice is never voided or re-amounted. So staff are told to bill a fee that is already covered, or one larger than what is still owed. The new test ('a payment made after the no-show was marked stops the charge', cardOnFile.test.ts:925) checks only that there is no PaymentIntent and the status is 'skipped'. It never checks that no fallback fires.
confirmed.trigger: Rate $400, deposit $100 paid, 50% fee. A no-show is marked and invoice PLS-x for $100 is pending. Within 15 minutes the client pays the $300 balance on the public checkout page: settlePayment only blocks 'cancelled', so amountPaidCents becomes 400. At the claim, paid (400) >= fee (200), so skip() runs and feeFallback tells staff and the client that a $100 invoice is to be sent. If staff send it, the client pays $500 for a $400 session. A partial top-up gives the same result: paid $150 leaves $50 owed, but staff are told to send $100.
confirmed.fix: In _claimFeeCharge, before autoChargeDecision, compute owed = feeStillOwedCents(fee, paidTowardSession(session)). If owed is 0, patch autoCharge skipped ('paid since the no-show') and void the draft invoice, with no feeFallback. If owed < inv.amountCents, patch amountCents and the line item to owed, then continue. Extend the test at cardOnFile.test.ts:925 to assert there is no 'Send invoice' insight and no session.no_show_fee notification.
confirmed.skepticReason: _claimFeeCharge passes paidCents: paidTowardSession(session) (cardOnFile.ts:392). When autoChargeDecision refuses with 'the client already paid at least the fee' or 'charge is more than the fee less what the client already paid' (cardConsent.ts:130-135), line 397 calls skip(), which calls feeFallback (cardOnFile.ts:356). That inserts the 'Send invoice X' insight, the auto_charge_failed activity and the team email. Because the session is still no_show (line 464), it also emails the client 'invoice to follow' for the unchanged inv.amountCents. The trigger can happen: settlePayment (payments.ts:120) refuses only 'cancelled', so a balance payment on a no_show session (or a Stripe checkout settling late) raises amountPaidCents. The test at cardOnFile.test.ts:925-938 asserts only that there is no PI and the status is 'skipped'. No money moves automatically, but staff are told to bill a fee that is covered or partly covered, and the client gets a false notice. Only a staff action creates the double bill, hence minor.

confirmed.title: Undo then re-mark the no-show: the fee is never auto-charged, and the only invoice tells staff to void it
confirmed.problem: undoNoShowCharge sets the fee invoice's autoCharge to 'skipped' but leaves the invoice as a live draft, with an activity line saying 'void it if the fee no longer applies'. If staff then mark the session no_show again, wasActive is true, so assessNoShowShield runs. But createCancellationFeeInvoice's alreadyBilled guard (sessions.ts:530) sees the old non-void fee invoice and returns null. invoiceId is null, so no charge is scheduled, noShowFeeInvoiceId is not refreshed, and the client is immediately emailed 'invoice to follow'. A genuine no-show with a valid agreement is never charged. Staff were last told to void the only invoice, and doing so drops the fee entirely.
confirmed.trigger: Switch on, card agreed, session started. Staff mark No-show, think better of it 2 minutes later and set Confirmed (the charge is cancelled), then confirm the client never came and mark No-show again. Nothing is ever charged, and invoice PLS-x still carries autoCharge 'skipped: no-show undone by staff'.
confirmed.fix: In assessNoShowShield, when createCancellationFeeInvoice returns null, look up an existing draft fee invoice for this session whose autoCharge.status is 'skipped' with the undo message. Reuse it: set noShowFeeInvoiceId, set autoCharge to pending with at = now, and schedule chargeFee after NO_SHOW_CHARGE_DELAY_MS, provided autoChargeDecision allows it and the amount still equals feeStillOwedCents. The alternative is to void A in undoNoShowCharge. Add an undo-then-re-mark test.
confirmed.skepticReason: undoNoShowCharge (sessions.ts:702-714) only sets autoCharge 'skipped' and leaves invoice A a live draft whose label contains 'fee'. On the re-mark, applyStatus:772 sees wasActive true (status is confirmed), so assessNoShowShield runs. createCancellationFeeInvoice's alreadyBilled check (sessions.ts:530-536) finds A and returns null. The patch at line 620 is skipped, and autoCharge = decision.charge && invoiceId !== null is false (line 641), so nothing is scheduled. Line 653 then emails the client 'invoice to follow'. No insight tells staff to send A, and the last activity told them to void it. A genuine no-show with valid consent is never auto-charged.

confirmed.title: The amount already paid ignores money paid on a session-linked invoice, so a completed and paid session re-marked as a no-show is charged the fee again
confirmed.problem: paidTowardSession counts only session.amountPaidCents and the deposit flag. Paying a session's invoice (invoicePay.settleInvoice, or a manual mark-paid) does not update session.amountPaidCents. 'completed' counts as active in applyStatus (wasActive), so moving a completed session to no_show runs assessNoShowShield. createCancellationFeeInvoice's guard ignores the paid completion invoice because its label has no 'fee'. The fee is then computed crediting only the deposit and auto-charged 15 minutes later. This breaks the owner rule 'never more than the fee minus everything the client has already paid for that session'.
confirmed.trigger: The automation cron auto-completes a session (automation.ts:109), and createCompletionInvoice drafts the $300 balance, which the client pays by link. Later a manager corrects the status to No-show (for example, the cron completed a session the client never attended, or a mis-click that is not undone within 15 minutes). With a 100% fee: paid is 100 (the deposit only), so $300 is charged to the saved card on top of the $300 invoice the client already paid.
confirmed.fix: In assessNoShowShield and _claimFeeCharge, add the sum of paid non-fee invoices for the session (by_artist filtered on sessionId, as createCompletionInvoice does) to the paid amount, or refuse the auto-charge when one exists. Add a 'completed and paid by invoice, then no-show' test.
confirmed.skepticReason: paidTowardSession (cardConsent.ts:43-49) reads only amountPaidCents and the deposit. invoicePay.settleInvoice and invoices.ts never update session.amountPaidCents (git grep finds no amountPaidCents in either). applyStatus:772 treats 'completed' as active, and setStatus has no transition guard, so completed→no_show runs assessNoShowShield. The completion invoice's line item is '<title> - balance' (sessions.ts:505), so createCancellationFeeInvoice's 'fee' label check (line 534) does not block. autoChargeDecision passes because now >= startTime, and the charge runs after 15 minutes. One correction: the cron auto-complete (automation.ts:108) patches the status directly and does NOT call createCompletionInvoice, so the trigger needs a manual completion (applyStatus:827) whose invoice was then paid. The path holds, but it needs staff to mark a completed, paid session as no-show and leave it for 15 minutes.

confirmed.title: A payment made after the no-show stops the charge but tells staff to bill the fee and tells the client an invoice will follow
confirmed.problem: Round 2 added paidCents: paidTowardSession(session) to the claim, so a payment made during the 15-minute window makes autoChargeDecision refuse ('the client already paid at least the fee' or 'charge is more than the fee less what the client already paid'). That refusal goes through skip(), which calls feeFallback (cardOnFile.ts:424-465). feeFallback inserts the 'Send invoice X: the no-show fee was not charged' insight, emails the team 'send invoice X to collect the fee', and, because the session is still no_show, emails the client that a fee invoice will follow. The invoice still holds the old amount (amountCents fixed at assessment), so staff are told to bill a fee the client has already covered, fully or partly. The test 'a payment made after the no-show was marked stops the charge' checks only that no PaymentIntent is created and the status is 'skipped'. It never checks the insight or the emails, so R2-01's PASS hides this.

Within 15 minutes the client pays the $200 balance from the pay link (settlePayment refuses only 'cancelled', not 'no_show'). At the claim, paid 200 >= fee 100, so skip() runs feeFallback. confirmed.fix: Same single fix as index 2: on a refusal caused by what was paid, skip without feeFallback, and void the invoice or re-amount it to feeStillOwedCents. Assert there is no insight and no client email in the test at cardOnFile.test.ts:925.
confirmed.skepticReason: Duplicate of index 2, traced the same way: cardOnFile.ts:397 calls skip(), which calls feeFallback (424-466). The result is the 'Send invoice' insight, the team email, and a client 'invoice to follow' email for the stale inv.amountCents, after a payment made in the window covers the fee fully or partly. The R2-01 PASS claims only that the charge is stopped, and that is true (no PI). The test simply does not cover the fallback messaging, so I rate it minor rather than a false PASS.

confirmed.title: After an undo, re-marking the no-show never charges, emails the client 'invoice to follow' and counts the deposit twice

confirmed.title: A short booking payment now leaves the booking open to automatic forfeit, and the studio keeps everything the client paid
confirmed.problem: Round 2 records only what Stripe collected, so a client who paid exactly what their Checkout showed is left with !fullyPaid on a confirmed public booking. The client is told '$X is still due; the studio will be in touch about it', with no deadline and no pay link. The forfeit sweep (automation.ts:386-398) still cancels any confirmed public booking that is not fully paid inside 2 hours of start, and it emails the client that the money they paid 'is kept by the studio'. The balance reminder is sent once (balanceRemindedAt), so if it already went out, the client gets no further prompt. A staff price change the client never agreed to thus turns a completed payment into a cancelled booking and lost money. This is round 1's 'automatic effect from a staff action' and 'state that looks unpaid to a background job' class.
confirmed.trigger: Confirmed public booking: rate $300, $100 deposit paid, start in 3 hours. The client opens a $200 balance Checkout. Staff add a $100 add-on (rate becomes $400). The client pays $200. Pulse records $200 and emails 'the studio will be in touch'. At T-2h automation.ts:388-398 forfeits the booking and emails 'The $300 you paid is kept by the studio'.
confirmed.fix: When settlePayment returns shortCents > 0 on a public booking, do both of these: (1) send the client the remaining amount, the pay link `${appUrl()}/book/${org.slug}/checkout/${sessionId}` and the 'pay in full at least 2 hours before your start time' deadline, instead of 'the studio will be in touch'. Or clear balanceRemindedAt so the existing reminder sends again. (2) Stop the automatic forfeit for a short-paid booking: patch a session field such as shortPaidAt in the webhook branch (billingWebhooks.ts:238) and add `!s.shortPaidAt` to the forfeit condition at automation.ts:388. Also say in the 'Payment short' team email that staff decide what happens to the booking.
confirmed.skepticReason: Traced. settlePayment (convex/payments.ts:127-132) now records min(owed, collectedCents), so a Checkout opened before a reprice leaves paidTotal < rateCents and fullyPaid=false (:147). The client then gets 'is still due on this session; the studio will be in touch about it' (:187-188), with no deadline and no pay link. The team gets 'Payment short' (billingWebhooks.ts:249-255), which does not mention the coming forfeit. For a public booking, runAutomation reaches the forfeit block (automation.ts:388-394). Its only exemption is studioBilled (pricingHidden), so it cancels the booking at T-2h and emails 'The $X you paid is kept by the studio' (:412-414). The balance reminder is once only (balanceRemindedAt, :191/:195). If the client opened the Checkout from that reminder, nothing prompts them again. The repricing trigger is real: sessions.ts:1013 for add-ons and :855-901 for extend/reschedule. Confirmed bookings' Checkouts have no expires_at, per round 1. Context: forfeit after a staff reprice already exists for a booking that was paid in full and then repriced, so the root cause is wider than this branch. But in this exact path the client completed the Checkout they were shown, which used to stop the forfeit, and round 2 now sends them a message that hides the deadline. Round 1's H206-02 fix asked for 'fullyPaid and the reminders reflect it', not a silent forfeit, and no owner decision for #206 calls for this behavior.

confirmed.title: H206-04 is partly fixed
confirmed.problem: Retries were added (strayPayments.ts:201-220, three attempts with the same idempotency key), and a 15-minute sweep was added (crons.ts plus strayPayments.ts:311-337) that leaves unconfirmed rows refund_pending and alerts the team once. But the refund action itself still ends the harmful way: after the three quick retries (about 750ms in total) createRefund returns {failed, unconfirmed:true} (:219). applyOutcome then calls finishRefund(ok:false) (:251-252), which sets the row to the terminal refund_failed (:378) and runs alertRefundFailed, and that emails the client 'The studio has been asked to refund you in full' (:161-171). So a network error after Stripe already refunded still sends the client the wrong message. The row also stays refund_failed for good, because neither the sweep nor a later refund webhook touches a non-pending row (:375). The test at test.ts:385 does not check the client email.
confirmed.trigger: see round 1 finding H206-04
confirmed.fix: In `refund` (strayPayments.ts:230-231), when createRefund returns {kind:'failed', unconfirmed:true}, do not call _applyOutcome. Leave the row 'refund_pending' so that sweepStuck retries it after STUCK_AFTER_MS with the same idempotency key and sends the team alert once through _reportStuck. That matches what sweepStuck already does at :326-329. Then add an assertion to the 'Stripe never answers' test that the row stays refund_pending and that no payment.refund_failed notification goes to the client.
confirmed.skepticReason: Traced on origin/fix/high-booking-payments. The `refund` action (convex/strayPayments.ts:225-232) calls createRefund. After 3 thrown errors, createRefund returns {kind:'failed', unconfirmed:true} (:219). applyOutcome (:251-252) then calls finishRefund(ok:false, unconfirmed:true), which patches the row to the terminal 'refund_failed' (:378) and calls alertRefundFailed. The `unconfirmed` flag only changes the team text (:157). The client email (:161-171) still says 'The studio has been asked to refund you in full and will be in touch', even when Stripe already refunded the payment. The row is also final: finishRefund (:375) and markRefundInProgress (:263) only act on 'refund_pending', and _stuck (:302) only selects 'refund_pending'. So neither the sweep nor a later refund.updated (billingWebhooks.ts:194-200 into applyRefundUpdate) can move the row to 'refunded' or send the correct 'Refunded' email. The two paths also disagree: sweepStuck (:326-329) handles the same unconfirmed outcome by leaving the row pending and alerting the team once, but the first attempt does not. The test 'Stripe never answers' (highRiskBookingPaymentsRound2.test.ts, about :385) checks only the team body, not the client email. Round 1 already showed the harm is messaging only (no double refund: Stripe's idempotency key holds and a manual refund of an already-refunded charge fails), so this stays minor and does not reach major.

confirmed.title: A refund Stripe reports succeeded and later fails is silently ignored
confirmed.problem: applyRefundUpdate routes a refund.failed or charge.refund.updated event with status 'failed' to finishRefund. finishRefund returns early unless the row is still refund_pending, so after a refund has succeeded (row 'refunded', client already emailed 'we refunded ... in full') a later failure changes nothing and alerts nobody. The webhook still marks the event processed as handled (applyRefundUpdate returns true at :293-294). Stripe documents that a refund can move from succeeded to failed, for example when the card was closed.
confirmed.trigger: A late payment on a released booking is refunded and Stripe returns 'succeeded', so the row is set to refunded and the client is told. Days later Stripe sends refund.failed for that refund. Pulse ignores it. The client never gets the money and the studio is not told.
confirmed.fix: In applyRefundUpdate (strayPayments.ts:293), when row.status === 'refunded' and the incoming status is 'failed' or 'canceled', patch the row to { status: 'refund_failed', error: `Stripe refund ${status} after it succeeded` }. Then send a team-only alert to refund by hand, and optionally a corrected client message, instead of going through finishRefund's refund_pending guard.
confirmed.skepticReason: Traced. billingWebhooks.ts:194-200 sends refund.updated, refund.failed and charge.refund.updated to applyRefundUpdate. For a row whose stored refundId matches (strayPayments.ts:292), applyRefundUpdate calls applyOutcome with a 'failed' outcome (:293). That calls finishRefund(ok:false), which returns at :375 because the row is already 'refunded'. Nothing is patched and nobody is alerted. applyRefundUpdate still returns true, so the event is marked processed under its real type (billingWebhooks.ts:199) and looks handled. No other path reads 'refunded' rows. A refund can move from succeeded to failed, but that is Stripe-side behavior, and whether these events are subscribed for connected accounts is endpoint configuration outside the repo. The code gap itself holds. It is rare, so minor.

confirmed.title: Voiding then deleting an invoice turns the void fix's automatic refund back into a silent hold of the client's money
confirmed.problem: invoices.remove now refuses sent, viewed and overdue invoices and tells the studio to void instead, but it still deletes a void invoice at once, and the UI shows Delete for void rows. Invoice Checkouts have no expires_at, so a pay link opened before the void stays payable for 24 hours. If the void invoice is then deleted, a late payment takes the deleted-target path (billingWebhooks.ts:312), which records an 'unmatched' needs_review row with no refund and no message to the client. A payment on the same invoice if not deleted would be auto-refunded as void_invoice with the client told. This is the duplicate-invoice case H206-01 targeted, reached in two clicks.
confirmed.trigger: The studio voids duplicate invoice A while the client has its Checkout open, then deletes A (now allowed). The client pays A. The money sits on the studio's account as needs_review, nothing is refunded, and the client is never told.
confirmed.fix: In invoices.remove, also refuse status 'void', at least within 24h of the void (store voidedAt, or check _creationTime of the void activity). Drop 'void' from the Delete condition in invoice-actions.tsx and invoice-table.tsx. Alternatively, keep the deletion as a soft delete so the webhook still finds a void row and refunds through the void_invoice path.
confirmed.skepticReason: Traced. invoices.remove (convex/invoices.ts:373-376) refuses only sent, viewed and overdue, so a 'void' invoice is deleted at once. invoice-actions.tsx and invoice-table.tsx now show Delete for draft, void and paid. Invoice Checkouts are created without expires_at (invoicePay.ts payViaStripe, checkout.sessions.create with no expires_at), so a link opened before the void stays payable for up to 24h. Once the row is deleted, the webhook takes the deleted-target path (billingWebhooks.ts:310-314 into recordDeletedTargetPayment :132-150). That records reason 'unmatched' (needs_review) with no refund and no client message. A void invoice that still exists is auto-refunded as 'void_invoice' with a client email (:324-332). So voiding and then deleting undoes the void fix's refund. Not fully silent: recordStrayPayment notifies the team (strayPayments.ts:111-117), so this is minor.

confirmed.title: Paying the prepaid-adjusted balance on the public checkout records the full cash balance, so hours are never drawn and the studio is paid short
confirmed.problem: Round 2 made booking._chargeContext (booking.ts:1347) subtract the prepaid cover, so Stripe charges only rate - amountPaid - cover. The webhook then calls settlePayment (billingWebhooks.ts:282) with only the kind. settlePayment works out the amount from outstanding() (payments.ts:81-90, 118), which ignores the cover, and never reads Stripe's amount_total. It records the whole cash balance as paid: a payments row and amountPaidCents for money that never arrived, plus a 'paid in full' email. At completion, computeCover sees owed 0, so no hours come off. The studio has received only part of the price, the client keeps the hours, and the ledger is overstated. The deposit and full kinds have the same problem whenever the cover makes the charge smaller than the recorded amount. The sheet's PaymentPanel (payment-panel.tsx, via bookingMoney) and payments.record also ignore the cover: the same sheet shows 'Paid in full' in one row and a 'Balance · $240' record button in another.
confirmed.trigger: A public session costs $300 for 3h, and a $60 deposit is paid. Staff choose a block with 2h left, so the cover is $200. The client opens the checkout, sees a $40 balance and pays $40 by card. The webhook records a $240 'balance' payment and sets amountPaidCents to 30000. Staff complete the session: 0h come off the block and nothing is invoiced. The studio got $100 cash for a $300 session, and the client still has 2h.
confirmed.fix: In the connected-account checkout branch of billingWebhooks.handle, pass obj.amount_total to settlePayment and record min(amount_total, outstanding) instead of recomputing. Also subtract prepaidCoverCents in outstanding() (or in settlePayment's caller) so payments.record and PaymentPanel ask for the same net amount. Add a convex-test: block with partial cover, a payViaStripe balance webhook, then completion, expecting amountPaidCents = rate - cover and the hours drawn.
confirmed.skepticReason: I traced the trigger and it holds. booking.ts:1347 _chargeContext computes paid = amountPaidCents + prepaidCoverCents, and payViaStripe (booking.ts:1375) charges balanceCents = rate - paid - cover. The webhook (billingWebhooks.ts:280-286) calls settlePayment with only {sessionId, kind, provider, reference}. settlePayment (payments.ts:117-118) takes amountCents from outstanding(), which is rate - amountPaid with no cover, and never reads obj.amount_total. Then it patches amountPaidCents = rate and sends 'Paid in full'. For a $300/3h session with $60 paid and 2h on the block: computeCover gives perHour 100, owed 240, exact 2, not coversAll, value 200. Stripe charges $40 and the ledger records $240. At completion computeCover finds owed = 300 - 300 = 0 and returns null (packages.ts:854), so no hours are drawn. The studio gets $100 cash and the client keeps 2h. Deposit kind: Stripe charges min(deposit, net balance) while the webhook records min(deposit, gross balance), so it has the same mismatch.

confirmed.title: Public checkout charges the balance net of prepaid cover, but the webhook records the full balance as paid, so the hours are never drawn
confirmed.problem: Round 2 subtracts prepaidCoverCents from the amount the public checkout charges (booking.ts:1347-1352 _chargeContext, used by payViaStripe at booking.ts:1376). The webhook then calls settlePayment (billingWebhooks.ts:282), which recomputes the amount from outstanding() (payments.ts:81-93) without the cover. It inserts a Stripe payment row for the larger amount and sets amountPaidCents to the full rate. At completion computeCover sees owed 0 (packages.ts:852-853), so no hours come off. The client has paid only the uncovered part in cash and keeps the prepaid hours, while the ledger and 'Paid in full' notices claim cash that Stripe never collected. The deposit kind has the same mismatch when the cover leaves less than the deposit (Stripe charges min(deposit, net balance); the webhook records min(deposit, gross balance)).

confirmed.title: Editing or removing an entry in a period already posted changes nothing in the ledger, and moving its clock-in into the next period posts those hours a second time

When a correction moves an entry's clockInAt across a period boundary, the hours stay in the old period's posted row and are counted again by the next period's post. That post sees no overlap, because the windows are adjacent. This is money counted without subtracting what was already posted.
confirmed.trigger: Weekly periods, Mon to Sun. Week 1 is posted and includes Eli's punch from Sun 22:00 to Mon 02:00 (4h, filed under week 1 by clock-in). So week 2's post never sees week 1's row, overlaps stays false, and week 2 posts the moved entry's full pay. adjustEntry (:270-330) lets clockInAt cross the boundary without checking whether the entry's original window is already posted, and removeEntry never checks either. Week 1's ledger row keeps the old amount. The overPosted warning only appears if someone re-posts week 1 exactly. The owner's round 2 decision only promises that re-posting the same period does not double count, so cross-period double counting is outside what was fixed. confirmed.title: Self clock-in can be backdated onto a manual entry, so the same hours are paid twice despite the new overlap guard

The offline queue that punchedAt exists for therefore produces exactly the overlap H208-06 was meant to stop.

Eli's phone reconnects and sends clockIn with at=9:00, which opens an entry from 9:00. He clocks out at 17:00, and payroll pays 8h + 2h for 8h worked.

If clamping changed the time, note it in tellManagers. Apply the same guard in clockOut, so a backdated close cannot reach into a later manual entry.

Reproduced in order: (1) the manager adds a manual entry 9:00-11:00 at 11:00, and refuseOverlap finds nothing because the phone's punch has not arrived; (2) the queued clockIn arrives with at=9:00 and opens an entry from 9:00; (3) clockOut at 17:00. postToExpenses then pays 8h + 2h. confirmed.title: H209-01 is partly fixed
confirmed.problem: A single save is now blocked. convex/lib/splitSigning.ts:151-173 clears a signed row's signature when its email changes. convex/splitSheets.ts:213-224 refuses an email or share change from anyone but the studio owner once someone has signed, and :228-232 reopens the sheet to 'sent'. Two paths still get around the owner rule. (a) Two saves: a non-owner first changes a name or role, which is a term change and is allowed. That clears every signature and sets the sheet to 'sent'. On the next save, `anyoneSigned` (:213-214) reads only the current rows and status, finds nobody signed, and lets the non-owner change the email or share. (b) A marked sheet: the rows on a sheet the owner marked signed on paper carry no signatures. A non-owner can call `setStatus` (:331-332), or `upsert` with a `status`, to move it out of marked_by_studio, and the email and share checks no longer apply. See new finding 1.

confirmed.fix: Same as item 1. Make the gate historical. In upsert, compute anyoneSigned as isSheetExecuted(existing.status) || any row signed/signedAt || existing.markedAt !== undefined || (await ctx.db.query("splitSignatureHistory").withIndex("by_sheet", q => q.eq("splitSheetId", existing._id)).first()) !== null. In setStatus, refuse a non-owner who moves a marked_by_studio sheet to another status. Add tests run as u_mgr for both two-step sequences, each expecting CAPABILITY_DENIED.
confirmed.skepticReason: Traced on origin/fix/high-split-signatures. The single-save path is closed: with any signature or an executed status, an email or share change by a non-owner throws (convex/splitSheets.ts:213-224). (a) The two-save path still works. Save 1, a role-only edit: lib/splitSigning.ts:136-139 sets termsChanged, :153-162 leaves sharesChanged and emailChanged false, so the owner gate at :215 does not fire. :183-184 blanks every row to signed:false, and splitSheets.ts:228-232 moves the sheet to 'sent'. Save 2: `anyoneSigned` (:213-214) now reads status 'sent' and rows with no signed/signedAt, so it is false, and the email or share change goes through for a non-owner. (b) The marked-sheet path also works. setStatus (:319-332) checks only `splitsheet.edit` and patches marked_by_studio to 'sent'/'draft' without clearing markedAt. Once no row carries a signature, the next upsert passes the gate. (A single upsert that passes both `status` and an email change is still blocked, because the gate reads existing.status. So this also takes two calls.) The owner's Round 2 decision for #209 reads 'only the owner can change a contributor's email or share once anyone has signed', and the code comment at :211-212 includes a marked sheet. So round 1's H209-01 harm is still reachable. This is the same defect as item 1.

confirmed.title: The owner-only rule for emails and shares can be bypassed by first clearing the signatures or unmarking the sheet
confirmed.problem: `anyoneSigned` (splitSheets.ts:213-214) reads only the current status and rows: an executed status, or a row with `signed`/`signedAt`. Two actions open to any `splitsheet.edit` holder (manager, producer, agency roles) set both to 'not signed'. (1) A name or role change counts as a term change and is not owner-gated. It clears every signature into splitSignatureHistory and reopens the sheet to 'sent'. (2) `setStatus` (:324-332) can move a marked_by_studio sheet back to 'sent' or 'draft', and so can `upsert` with a `status` argument (:233). The rows on a sheet marked signed on paper carry no signatures. After either action, the next `upsert` passes the owner check, so a non-owner can re-key a contributor's email or change shares. This is the H209-01 harm, and it defeats the owner's round 2 decision. Since H209-04, co-signers re-signing through their links can no longer see emails, so they cannot notice that the address changed.
confirmed.trigger: Alice and Bob signed by link and the sheet is fully_executed. A producer on the studio account edits Alice's role from 'Songwriter' to 'Writer' in the Splits tab and saves. This is allowed: every signature is cleared and the status becomes 'sent'. The producer then edits Alice's email to producer@x.com and saves, which is now allowed because no row is signed. The producer clicks Re-send signing links, signs Alice's link at producer@x.com, and Bob re-signs because the terms changed. The sheet executes, and every new royalty line credits Alice's master share to producer@x.com. A sheet the owner marked on paper is bypassed the same way: the producer calls `splitSheets.setStatus({ id, status: "sent" })`, then changes an email or share in one save.
confirmed.fix: In upsert (convex/splitSheets.ts:213), set anyoneSigned = isSheetExecuted(existing.status) || existing.contributors.some(c => c.signed || signedByPerson(c)) || existing.markedAt !== undefined || (await ctx.db.query("splitSignatureHistory").withIndex("by_sheet", q => q.eq("splitSheetId", existing._id)).first()) !== null. In setStatus (:324), when sheet.status === "marked_by_studio" and the caller is not a studio_member owner, throw CAPABILITY_DENIED. Do the same in upsert when `status` is given for a marked sheet. Add two u_mgr tests: a role change then an email change, and setStatus('sent') then an email change. Both should expect CAPABILITY_DENIED.
confirmed.skepticReason: Path is real and nothing else guards it. A role-only change matches sameTerms (lib/splitSigning.ts:89-96), so termsChanged=true while sharesChanged and emailChanged stay false (:153-162). The owner gate (splitSheets.ts:215) therefore passes. Every signature is cleared into splitSignatureHistory (:243-246 → keepClearedSignatures; lib :183-184), and the status goes to 'sent' (:228-232). On the next upsert, anyoneSigned (:213-214) is false because 'sent' is not executed and every row is signed:false with no signedAt. A non-owner can then change an email or share; the email change is logged but not gated. For the marked sheet: setStatus (:324-332) is capability-only, does not check the owner role and does not clear markedAt. It moves marked_by_studio to 'sent', and rows on a paper-marked sheet often carry no signatures, so a later email or share change passes the gate. The fix can rely on markedAt, because nothing clears it (only written at :395). It can also rely on splitSignatureHistory, which has a by_sheet index (schema.ts:1901). Severity stays major, not critical. The money only moves after every other signer re-signs and someone signs the new address's link, and the actor must already hold splitsheet.edit. Still, the owner's Round 2 rule for #209 is defeated, and round 1 rated the same harm major.
